voice.ref_text: So, we are attacking a 31.6 trillion cross-border market.

lines: Every lender asks one question: can I trust this borrower? On a new chain, nobody can answer.
A signature proves nothing. A bridge needs a committee. An oracle brings back the middleman you were trying to remove.
So Hana doesn't ask anyone to vouch. We import the record itself, and let Creditcoin verify it on chain with a cryptographic proof.
And we didn't build one app on top of it. We built two, deliberately different, so the registry has to behave like a primitive.
Everything from here is live. Real contracts, deployed and verified on Creditcoin's test network. Nothing in this demo is a rendering.
These addresses aren't copied onto a slide. The page reads them straight from the deployment record, so they cannot drift.
Here's a wallet that has never borrowed on Creditcoin. But it has years of lending history on Ethereum.

Seven eighty-six. Nobody typed that in. It came from fourteen completed loans and forty on-time payments on Ethereum, proved across by a Merkle inclusion proof, and verified by a precompile. No oracle. No committee.
And this is what makes it a business. One score, two unrelated products. Retail instalments in dollars, and a node operator credit line in a staking token.
So let's spend it. A real purchase, underwritten against that imported limit.
No card. No application. No bank in the middle. Just pay with Hana.

Four instalments. And this is a real transaction, signed and broadcast to Creditcoin while you watch. Not a mock. Watch the available credit fall, because the loan genuinely drew against it. That decision was made by a contract reading one number.
The loan is live on chain. Four instalments, the first one due, and the merchant settled from a vault.
Now the second product. Same wallet, same score, completely different risk. A credit line that stakes itself and repays out of yield.
Claiming that yield pays the debt down. Real transaction, real yield, a real block. This is the credit line Creditcoin published on its own roadmap.
Two applications, one registry, one public interface. Any contract on Creditcoin can underwrite against this today. That is a primitive.
